With logits s=cos(h,e)/τ, uncorrected candidate cross-entropy is −s₊+log(exp(s₊)+Σ₁⁶⁴exp(sⱼ)): discrimination among 65 sampled entries. An importance-estimated partition instead uses exp(s₊)+Σexp(sⱼ)/(64qᵤ(j)), with qᵤ conditional on history filtering. Uniform sampling over Mᵤ eligible negatives gives multiplier Mᵤ/64. This estimates the eligible partition; finite-sample log-loss/gradients remain biased, and excluded items cannot be recovered by importance weighting. Subtracting an identical log-q correction from every candidate cancels; distinguish that convention from correcting sampled negatives while retaining the positive exactly. [TensorFlow sampling reference](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf)

Generalized BCE uses independent sigmoid terms with a calibration-adjusted positive term, rather than a shared softmax denominator. gSASRec combines gBCE with more negatives to mitigate sampling-induced overconfidence; it is not importance-corrected softmax. Recommended controls: hold architecture, initialization, batches, optimizer, filtering and 64 negatives fixed; compare BCE/gBCE/candidate CE/corrected softmax under identical logits, then independently vary embedding normalization, temperature and negative count. Match loss reductions and tuning budgets; temperature preserves fixed-model rankings but changes training gradients. [gSASRec paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192)

Training duplicates increase an item's weight: retain multiplicities for an explicitly with-replacement estimator, or sample without replacement and use matching inclusion probabilities; silently deduplicating changes the estimator. Exclude padding and positive collisions. Keep evaluation's 99 unique negatives, users and seed identical across ablations; select by four-category macro validation HR@10, reporting category results and paired uncertainty. Never modify the pinned evaluator or interpret sampled HR as full-catalog HR: sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons. [Sampled-metrics study](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)
